Package Refactoring & Data Reorganization

This document records the architectural refactoring, data reorganization, and automation enhancements introduced in metabr (v0.2.4).

1. Background & Motivation

As metabolomics datasets in the Kibbey Lab / Attie Lab systems genetics studies expanded across study cohorts (Founder plasma, Diversity Outbred liver, and Diversity Outbred plasma), metabr needed to transition from project-specific, one-off analysis scripts to a standardized, parameterized data processing pipeline.

Key goals of the refactoring:

  1. Standardize Data Layout: Replace ad-hoc root folders with a unified, dated directory hierarchy under data/"QC Batch Correction".
  2. Unify QC Automation: Transition from separate annual scripts (QC_Automation_2023.Rmd, QC_Automation_2025.Rmd) to a single parameterized pipeline (QC_Automation.Rmd).
  3. Harmonize Function APIs: Ensure consistency in argument naming (e.g. exclude_first vs. legacy flags) and handle missing plate CF imputations.
  4. Establish Developer Infrastructure: Implement standard agentic instructions (AGENTS.md), a living developer guide (DEVELOPER.md), and comprehensive pkgdown vignettes.

Data Cohort Summaries

Batch Date Cohort Tissue Data Available Naming Conventions & Notes
20231127 Founder mice Plasma Raw + Corrected (Hand) + Automated Initial benchmark study. Used leading # folder prefixes (#Founder_Plasma_Raw_Data/, #Founder_Plasma_Batch_Corrected_Data/). Evaluated automated pipeline vs. manual human curation using hand_auto().
20251112 Diversity Outbred Liver Raw only + Automated Relies entirely on automated pipeline (2025_Nov_Automated/). Introduces (in) input indicators and min1000 minimum peak area threshold flags.

3. QC Pipeline Architecture & Unification

Historical Scripts vs. Parameterized Pipeline

Prior to refactoring, each new data transfer used a dedicated script with hardcoded paths. The new architecture provides both historical traceability and a single parameterized entry point:

  1. QC_Automation.Rmd (Unified Pipeline):
    • Configured with params$batch_date (defaults to "20261020").
    • Dynamically resolves directory paths, filename conventions, and assay types.
    • Automatically passes exclude_first = TRUE for RP_Pos mode to drop initial column conditioning outliers.
    • Dynamically checks for reference hand curation and runs hand_auto() diagnostics only when available.
    • Implements non-zero file size guards to handle empty or placeholder files gracefully without throwing execution errors.
  2. Historical Reference Scripts:
    • QC_Automation_2023.Rmd: Preserved analysis trace for Founder Plasma benchmarking.
    • QC_Automation_2025.Rmd: Preserved analysis trace for DO Liver automation.

How to Run the Parameterized Pipeline 

library(metabr)

# 1. Run for default batch (20261020)
rmarkdown::render("QC_Automation.Rmd")

# 2. Or re-run any historical batch
rmarkdown::render("QC_Automation.Rmd", params = list(batch_date = "20251112"))
rmarkdown::render("QC_Automation.Rmd", params = list(batch_date = "20231127"))

4. Documentation & Infrastructure Overhaul

The documentation infrastructure was restructured for maintainability and automated publishing:

  • AGENTS.md: Standardized system instructions following the Pure R Package / Shiny App CRAFT archetype, including explicit rules governing version control and testing.
  • DEVELOPER.md: Root architectural developer guide with Mermaid flowcharts, function tables, QC formulas, and workflow notebook descriptions.
  • README.md: Updated with Step 0 data setup, Option 1 parameterized pipeline execution, and Option 2 step-by-step QC functions.
  • vignettes/devel_guide/:
    • index.Rmd: Ecosystem overview and local development quick start.
    • qc_pipeline.Rmd: Mathematical correction formulation, medRt untargeted handling, and hand_auto() diagnostics.
    • data_ingestion.Rmd: Schema definitions, input loaders, and write_metab() export rules.
    • deployment.Rmd: CI/CD architecture and GitHub Pages publishing workflow (moved and converted from inst/doc/devel_guide.md).
    • refactor.Rmd: This refactoring and reorganization guide.
  • _pkgdown.yml: Configured with Bootstrap 5, dynamic Mermaid JS v10 header rendering, and custom Developer Guide dropdown menu.

5. Recipe for Adding New Data Batches

When receiving a new metabolomics data drop from the mass spectrometry core:

  1. Create Timestamped Directory: Create a new dated folder: data/"QC Batch Correction"/<YYYYMMDD>/.
  2. Deposit Raw Data: Place raw El-MAVEN CSV exports into an input folder (e.g., Raw/ or <Cohort>_Raw/).
  3. Document in datasets.Rmd: Add an entry to datasets.Rmd detailing the cohort, tissue, mode files, and OneDrive source link.
  4. Update QC_Automation.Rmd Dispatcher: Add the date mapping in configure_paths chunk of QC_Automation.Rmd matching the new filenames.
  5. Execute and Verify: Run rmarkdown::render("QC_Automation.Rmd", params = list(batch_date = "<YYYYMMDD>")).
  6. Inspect Exported Matrices: Verify generated CSV files in data/"QC Batch Correction"/<YYYYMMDD>/Automated/.
